Clin Pharmacokinet 2004; 43: 1127–56. Antiepileptics. Retrospective review of outcomes in children treated for acute lymphoblastic leukaemia indicated that long- term antiepileptic therapy increased the clearance of several an- tileukaemic drugs and reduced the efficacy of therapy.1 1. Relling MV, et al. Adverse effect of anticonvulsants on efficacy of chemotherapy for acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. Lancet 2000; 356: 285–90. Antivirals. The potential for interaction between antiretrovirals and antineoplastics has been reviewed.1 Although clinical evi- dence of interactions is scanty, various HIV-protease inhibitors and NNRTIs can inhibit or induce cytochrome P450 isoenzymes, and thus have the potential to interact with a number of antineo- plastics including taxanes, vinca alkaloids, and cyclophospha- mide. 1. Antoniou T, Tseng AL. Interactions between antiretrovirals and antineoplastic drug therapy. Clin Pharmacokinet 2005; 44: 111–45. Effects on other drugs. Antineoplastics have been reported to affect a number of drugs including: • digoxin (reduced absorption, see p.1262) • oral anticoagulants (increased or decreased effect, see Warfa- rin, p.1429) • phenytoin (increased or decreased effect, see p.499) • suxamethonium (prolonged effect, see p.1911) • vaccines (decreased response, see p.2202). Herbal medicines. The potential for interactions between an- tineoplastics and herbal medicines has been reviewed.1 There is a general lack of information and reports, and warnings are large- ly based on theory and extrapolation from herbal interactions with other drugs. 1. Sparreboom A, et al. Herbal remedies in the United States: po- tential adverse interactions with anticancer agents. J Clin Oncol 2004; 22: 2489–2503. Pharmacokinetics Many antineoplastics have intra- and interindividual pharmacokinetic variability that can be influenced by a number of factors. Patient age, disease state, and drug interactions can affect drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. Genetic polymorphisms also affect drug disposition and are under investigation, but the clinical use of such information is currently limited. Various methods have been tried or are being investigated as ways of tailoring initial drug dosage and therapeutic drug monitoring for individual patients in order to improve treatment efficacy and minimise toxicity.
